newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-MESSIER TIES BOSSY FOR 10TH ON ALL-TIME GOALS LIST.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-MESSIER TIES BOSSY FOR 10TH ON ALL-TIME GOALS LIST.

text.p: Mark Messier tied former New York Islander Mike Bossy for 10th place on the NHL's all-time goals list with a power-play tally midway through the third period to give the New York Rangers a 3-2 win over the Washington Capitals Wednesday.

Messier beat Olaf Kolzig with a wrist shot from the right circle with 8:47 remaining in the game for his his 573rd career goal and 34th of the season. Kolzig got a piece of the shot, but the puck found its way between his arm and body.
"It didn't go through my legs," said Kolzig. "It hit me right in the hip and I tried to squeeze it and it trickled through."
Washington held a 2-1 lead before Adam Graves tied it eight minutes into the second period.
Newly acquired Rick Tocchet and Adam Oates continued to pay dividends for the Capitals.

Tocchet gave Washington the 2-1 lead. It was his second goal with his new club. Oates, obtained in the same deal that brought Tocchet and goaltender Bill Ranford from the Bruins, assisted on the goal for his fourth point as a Capital.
Ranford, 3-1 in five starts with the Capitals, left the game in the second period after injuring a thumb. Kolzig came on and yielded the tying and winning goals.

Dale Hunter opened the scoring midway through the first period, but the Rangers tied it just over four minutes later on Wayne Gretzky's 19th goal of the season. It was only Gretzky's third goal in 29 games.
New York goalie Mike Richter stopped 25 shots, including a penalty shot by Ken Klee in the second period.
Esa Tikkanen and Russ Courtnall, acquired from Vancouver Saturday, made their Ranger debuts. Tikkanen assisted on Messier's goal.

In Anaheim, Jari Kurri scored the go-ahead goal and Guy Hebert made 38 saves as the Mighty Ducks extended their franchise-record unbeaten streak to nine game with a 2-1 victory over the Detroit Red Wings.
The second-period goal gave Kurri 1,369 career points, tying John Bucyk for 11th on the all-time list.
Teemu Selanne scored his team-leading 43rd goal for a 1-0 lead 70 seconds into the second period. Sergei Fedorov tallied for Detroit.
The Red Wings had been 6-0-5 in their previous 11 games.

In Hartford, Kent Manderville recorded his first career hat trick and Sami Kapanen scored on a penalty shot as the Whalers extended their unbeaten streak to four games with a 6-3 victory over the Boston Bruins.
"It's like Christmas morning when you're a kid opening presents, it's a lot of fun," Manderville said. "We got the two points and that's what's most important."

Robert Kron and Paul Ranheim also tallied for Hartford, 3-0-1 in its last four games The victory moved the Whalers three points ahead of the Capitals, Canadiens and Lightning, who are all tied for eighth place in the Eastern Conference.
Tim Sweeney, Brett Harkins and Sandy Moger scored power-play goals for Boston, last in the Eastern Conference.
In Colorado, Ronnie Stern's second goal of the game with 2:55 left in the third period snapped a tie and lifted the Calgary Flames to a 3-2 victory over the Avalanche.
Theo Fleury also tallied for Calgary. The win gave the Flames 65 points and kept them tied with Chicago for the final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
Peter Forsberg had a goal and an assist for Colorado, winless in three straight (0-2-1) for just the second time this season.
In Toronto, Denis Savard scored the tying and game-winning goals to lead the Chicago Blackhawks to a 3-2 win that snapped the Maple Leafs' season-high unbeaten streak at five games.
Chicago outshot Toronto 41-21 and won for just the second time (2-3-3) in its last eight games.

Mats Sundin made it 1-0 for Toronto 3:03 into the game but Ethan Moreau tied it for the Blackhawks in the second period before Sergei Berezin gave the Maple Leafs a 2-1 edge with 87 seconds left in the second.
In Phoenix, Stu Barnes scored his second goal of the game with 49 seconds remaining in regulation as the Pittsburgh Penguins rallied for a 5-5 tie with the Coyotes.

Pittsburgh led 3-2 entering the third period but Darrin Shannon and Keith Tkachuk scored to give Phoenix a 4-3 edge. Alex Hicks tallied for the Penguins just 11 seconds after Tkachuk, tying it at four.
Shannon's second goal of the game, with 9:33 remaining in regulation, gave the Coyotes a 5-4 lead.
Pittsburgh pulled goaltender Ken Wregget for an extra attacker in the final minute.

Ron Francis won a draw in the Phoenix zone and drew the puck back to Mario Lemieux, who faked a slap shot before feeding a perfect pass to the right side of the net, where a wide-open Barnes tapped the puck in for an easy goal.
Garry Valk and Fredrik Olausson also scored and Lemieux finished with three assists for Pittsburgh, 1-0-2 in its last three games following a 1-10 stretch.
